decisions.notes: quote_mismatch explained: the archived civicclerk PDF is the July 20, 2026 agenda/packet cover, not the July 6 minutes; pages 3-31 returned blank OCR (a scanned-but-not-text pdf), so the cited minutes quote cannot be checked against it — this is an extraction failure, not evidence of fabrication. A second archived file from the same portal (work/sources/AL/89962cd22fc4fb94.md) is the same July 20 agenda listing, also without the moratorium text. I ran an additional search and found an independent secondary source (citizenportal.ai, Aug 17 2026) that confirms a six-month moratorium was already in force by mid-August 2026, and the AL.com roundup dataset agrees on 7/6/2026 and six months. No source contradicts the date. I was not able to independently pull the actual July 6 minutes text within the search budget, so confidence is capped at moderate rather than high.

decisions.notes: I cannot reconcile the sources on which instrument, date and duration are actually in force. The archived Ordinance 1043-2026 text (180 days) matches the row's legal_basis and the Sept. 14/15 abc3340 amendment story, which also treats 1043-2026 and 180 days as current — so the row's legal_basis and duration are probably right. But the adoption date is genuinely contested: AL.com reports the ordinance as approved Aug. 10; WVTM13's contemporaneous report says Aug. 10 was only a first reading with a second reading set for Aug. 24; a Shelby County Reporter piece instead calls the base instrument 'Ordinance 1037-2026' with a 100-day (not 180-day) term and quotes a resident referencing 'June'; a mytownview.com AI summary says Ordinance 1043-2026 was 'rejected' on Aug. 10; and the Sept. 2026 amendment coverage has both a council member and the reporter referring to the original moratorium as adopted 'in June.' This is exactly the OLDER_INSTRUMENT risk the coordinator flagged — possibly an earlier June or Aug.-10 instrument that was later re-passed or renumbered as 1043-2026 on some other date — but I could not determine, within the search budget, which account is correct. The row already hedges with month-only precision ('2026-08'), which I think is the right call pending further research; I am not changing any field, only flagging the conflict for the coordinator. verify_resolutions below leaves the existing VERIFY marker in place as still unresolved, now with more (conflicting) detail attached.

verify_resolutions.note: The Sept. 14 amendment (3-1 vote, two projects exempted, data centers still covered) is independently confirmed by two abc3340 articles. But that same reporting introduces a NEW unresolved conflict over the base ordinance's true adoption date and number (Aug. 10 vs Aug. 24 vs 'June'; 1043-2026/180 days vs 1037-2026/100 days). The marker should stay.
